ActorOut.description:
Who placed an order, as the server recorded it.

``kind`` is ``human`` (the deployment operator), ``agent`` (a scoped key), ``strategy``
(the engine) or ``unknown``. ``id`` addresses that kind: the operator subject, the agent
key id, or the strategy id. It is null exactly when the kind is unknown, which is what a
row written before the actor was recorded reports. A client can never supply this.
ActorOut.title: ActorOut

AgentBucketCapIn.description:
Set one agent's cap. The cap is the most net cash that agent may deploy.

Nothing else is settable: the bucket has no balance to write, because its deployment
is the ledger's. An unknown field is refused (``422``), so a caller cannot smuggle a
balance or a different agent id into the body — the agent id is in the path.
AgentBucketCapIn.title: AgentBucketCapIn

AgentBucketOut.description:
One agent's bucket: the cap its owner set and what the ledger says it deployed.

``deployed_usd`` is the net cash this agent's journal legs moved, and
``available_usd`` is what is left of the cap (null when the cap is null, which no
stored row produces). A deployment above the cap is a legitimate state after a
lowering: it refuses new entries and never traps an exit.
AgentBucketOut.title: AgentBucketOut

AgentBucketsOut.description: Every agent whose owner set a cap. An uncapped agent is absent, not a zero row.
AgentBucketsOut.title: AgentBucketsOut

ApprovalDecisionIn.description: A person's decision. It carries a note, never an order: the stored intent executes.
ApprovalDecisionIn.title: ApprovalDecisionIn

ApprovalDecisionOut.description: The server's own risk evidence for an approval. Never text from the agent.
ApprovalDecisionOut.title: ApprovalDecisionOut

ApprovalIntentOut.description: The stored order request a person is approving, exactly as the agent proposed it.
ApprovalIntentOut.title: ApprovalIntentOut

ApprovalOut.description:
One agent order waiting for a person, and the record of what was decided.

``status`` is one declared lifecycle value and ``next_action`` names what a reader may
do in it (``approve_or_reject`` while pending, ``execute`` for the one claim an
approval takes, ``none`` once terminal). ``decided_by`` is the person; a null means no
person has decided yet.
ApprovalOut.title: ApprovalOut

ApprovalRejectIn.description: A rejection requires the person's reason.
ApprovalRejectIn.title: ApprovalRejectIn

AttributionRowOut.description: A token row plus its share of absolute realized PnL across tokens.
AttributionRowOut.title: AttributionRowOut

AutomationOut.description:
The per-user automation tier and the disclosure behind it.

``agent_orders`` is the plain-language consequence: ``wait_for_a_person`` under
``manual``, ``execute_automatically`` under ``full_auto``.
AutomationOut.title: AutomationOut

AutomationTierIn.description: Switch a user's automation tier. ``full_auto`` requires the acknowledgement.
AutomationTierIn.title: AutomationTierIn

BacktestIn.description: A backtest request. Exactly one of ``graph`` / ``strategy_id`` names the graph.
BacktestIn.title: BacktestIn

BuildSourceOut.description: The signed-provenance verdict, with a reason when the build is not official.
BuildSourceOut.title: BuildSourceOut

CandleOut.description: One closed OHLCV bar. Prices are decimal strings; unknown volume is null.
CandleOut.title: CandleOut

CostPreviewOut.description: The pre-trade cost sheet. Nulls are unknowns ("—"), never zeros.
CostPreviewOut.title: CostPreviewOut

DailyRealizedOut.description:
One UTC day of closed and fee-bearing ledger groups.

``realized_usd`` is already net of fees, so ``fees_usd`` is disclosure, not an
additional subtraction.
DailyRealizedOut.title: DailyRealizedOut

DiscoveryAppliedOut.description:
The floors and bounds this response was produced under.

They come from ``Settings`` where a field exists (`min_pair_age_minutes`,
`min_liquidity_usd`, `max_mark_age_seconds`); only the feed window is still a module
constant, and a Settings field for it is the documented follow-up. Echoing every bound
here means a reader never has to guess which ones produced the page.
DiscoveryAppliedOut.title: DiscoveryAppliedOut

DiscoveryCoverageOut.description:
What the pass saw and what it dropped, so a short feed is explainable.

``candidates`` is every row read, ``deduped`` is how many tokens remained, and
``dropped`` counts each rejection under the first reason that applied to it.
``chains`` is the adapter's per-chain coverage, carried through unchanged: a chain with
``reason == "error"`` or ``"no_seeds"`` means the source failed or was never asked, which
is not the same fact as a chain that answered and had nothing new. ``None`` means the
pass made no per-chain claim (a global search), never "every chain was fine".
DiscoveryCoverageOut.title: DiscoveryCoverageOut

DiscoveryMetricOut.description:
One displayed number, its source and the age of that observation.

``known`` is explicit so a client cannot read a missing value as a zero: ``value`` is
null exactly when nothing was measured, and then the source still says who was asked.
DiscoveryMetricOut.title: DiscoveryMetricOut

DiscoveryNewPairOut.description:
One new pair: the token, its ages, its numbers and its safety verdict.

``tradeable`` is true only with positive safety evidence. ``not_tradeable_reason`` says
why otherwise, and every metric names its own source and age.
DiscoveryNewPairOut.title: DiscoveryNewPairOut

DiscoverySafetyOut.description:
The safety evidence behind a row's ``tradeable`` flag.

``status`` is ``verified`` only with positive evidence. ``unknown`` is the honest state
of this build: no safety source exists, so ``reason`` names that
(``SAFETY_NOT_IMPLEMENTED``) and ``checked_at`` is null — never a timestamp that would
imply a check happened.
DiscoverySafetyOut.title: DiscoverySafetyOut

FundingOut.description:
The audit of a paper no-risk top-up, as persisted on the order.

Money stays a decimal string. ``cash_after_usd`` equals ``cash_before_usd`` on a
cap-refused order: nothing was funded.
FundingOut.title: FundingOut

GraphValidateIn.description:
The document is checked by the core validator, not by Pydantic here.

``Any`` is deliberate: a malformed document must produce the graph's own
``STRATEGY_GRAPH_INVALID`` envelope, not Pydantic's field-error list.
GraphValidateIn.title: GraphValidateIn

KillSwitchIn.description:
One switch, one step, in either direction.

Arming and releasing are symmetric: both accept an optional reason and both store it
when supplied. The reason is operator bookkeeping, not a protection for a key or an
outsider, so requiring it on release alone gated the owner's own trading.
KillSwitchIn.title: KillSwitchIn

KillSwitchOut.description: One flag, two levels: global applies to every caller, strategy to strategy intents.
KillSwitchOut.title: KillSwitchOut

LedgerEntryOut.description:
One append-only journal entry, exactly as persisted.

``wallet_id`` names the paper wallet a cash leg settled to when it was written. It is
null on every leg that is not cash (position, the `fees:USD` expense, PnL and equity
legs). The no-risk funding top-up *is* cash and carries the settlement wallet id
because it is booked as settlement capital; its ``funding:USD`` contra leg carries
none. A null is never given a wallet at read time: on a legacy cash row it means the
row predates wallet attribution, not that it settled nowhere.

``actor_kind`` and ``actor_id`` name the principal that placed the order this group
belongs to, copied onto each leg when it was written. A row written before the actor
was recorded reports ``unknown`` with a null id; that is never derived afterwards.

``bucket_id`` names the agent bucket a cash leg was drawn from or returned to. It is
null on a non-cash leg, a person's order, and every row that predates buckets. The
bucket's deployment is a replay of the rows that name it, never a stored balance.
LedgerEntryOut.title: LedgerEntryOut

MarketChainOut.description: One registered chain as the market monitor currently sees it.
MarketChainOut.title: MarketChainOut

MarketCoverageOut.description:
One chain's contribution to a discovery pass; counts are pre-slice.

``no_seeds`` means no address existed for the chain, so the pass did not ask the
provider and its population is unknown — never an empty observation.
MarketCoverageOut.title: MarketCoverageOut

MarketFiltersOut.description:
The validated filters actually applied to this request.

``unknown_excluded`` names every active filter that dropped a row because the
provider value was unknown. Unknown is never treated as zero.
MarketFiltersOut.title: MarketFiltersOut

MarketPopulationOut.description: What the discovery pass saw before this page was sliced from it.
MarketPopulationOut.title: MarketPopulationOut

MarketRowOut.description:
One live pair row with the contract's own source and read-time age.

``age_seconds`` and ``stale`` come from the row's ``SourceRef`` against the read
clock, not from a freshness flag the adapter wrote.
MarketRowOut.title: MarketRowOut

NewPairsOut.description:
The new-pairs read model: a bounded, deduplicated, safety-evidenced feed.

An empty ``rows`` list carries a ``reason`` code. ``tradeable_on_page`` counts the rows
of *this page* with positive safety evidence — ``total`` counts the population — which is
zero in this build; a client must render the per-row ``safety`` rather than inferring
from that count alone.
NewPairsOut.title: NewPairsOut

PaperAccountOut.description: The paper account read model. Equity is withheld when any open mark is unknown.
PaperAccountOut.title: PaperAccountOut

PaperAssetCompositionOut.description:
One asset's server-computed contribution to the paper account.

``share_pct`` is null whenever equity is incomplete or non-positive. Cash is the USD
settlement row (``kind = "cash"``); its value is always known, but its share is still
withheld while the equity denominator is unknown.
PaperAssetCompositionOut.title: PaperAssetCompositionOut

PaperChainCompositionOut.description:
One chain's server-computed total. Native quantity lives on the asset row.

``market_value_usd`` is null when any asset on the chain is unpriced: a partial chain
total is never presented as the chain's value.
PaperChainCompositionOut.title: PaperChainCompositionOut

PaperLimitsOut.description: Risk limits the UI may show. Never contains a token, database URL or secret.
PaperLimitsOut.title: PaperLimitsOut

PaperOrderIn.description:
A manual paper order.

Deliberately has no ``strategy_id``: strategy attribution is internal to the engine,
which reaches the order service through ``KillSwitchExecutor``. It also has no
``actor``: the placing principal is resolved from the authenticated caller and a body
that tries to supply it is refused. Unknown fields are refused (``422``, with the
field named in ``loc``), so a hand-written request can neither claim strategy or
principal attribution nor have a misspelt limit silently dropped. The refusal happens
before the quote or any journal write.
PaperOrderIn.title: PaperOrderIn

PaperPerformanceOut.description:
PAPER performance from the append-only ledger.

``trades`` counts fills (executions). ``wins``/``losses`` count closed sell groups
with a positive/negative net result; a breakeven close is in neither, so
``win_rate_pct`` is null when no close has a direction.
PaperPerformanceOut.title: PaperPerformanceOut

PaperUnpricedPositionOut.description: An open position whose mark is unknown: it is never valued at zero.
PaperUnpricedPositionOut.title: PaperUnpricedPositionOut

PaperWalletCompositionOut.description:
One wallet's contribution to equity: settled cash and its chain's positions.

``market_value_usd`` is null when any position on the wallet's chain is unpriced; the
chain is never valued at zero. ``settled_usd`` is always known because it is a ledger
sum. ``wallet_id`` is null only for the ``unallocated`` row that keeps positions on a
chain with no wallet from disappearing out of the total.
PaperWalletCompositionOut.title: PaperWalletCompositionOut

PaperWalletOut.description:
A paper wallet, or the unallocated cash bucket, and its ledger-derived cash.

The row stores no balance: ``balance_usd`` is the sum of the cash legs attributed to
it. ``mode`` travels with the number so a wallet read can never be mistaken for a live
balance. ``id`` is null only for the ``unallocated`` row, which keeps cash whose
attributed wallet id no longer has a row; it is a bucket, not a wallet, and it exists
so the list is a complete partition of ``cash_usd``.
PaperWalletOut.title: PaperWalletOut

PolicyFieldOut.description: One sizing field with its value, range and the description shown to the owner.
PolicyFieldOut.title: PolicyFieldOut

PolicyOut.description:
The trade-policy decision the order gate enforced (GH-107).

The limits are the snapshot taken when the order was placed, not a live lookup: a later
settings change must not rewrite what the order was measured against.
PolicyOut.title: PolicyOut

PolicyProfileOut.description: One named profile and every sizing field it bundles.
PolicyProfileOut.title: PolicyProfileOut

PolicyWarningOut.description: A strategy setting that the order gate would refuse under its profile.
PolicyWarningOut.title: PolicyWarningOut

PositionOut.description:
One open position, with the server's own verdict on its mark's freshness.

``mark_age_seconds`` is null when there is no usable observation, and ``mark_status``
says why, so no client has to re-derive staleness from a timestamp.
PositionOut.title: PositionOut

SignalAppliedOut.description: The filters and the bounds this response was produced under.
SignalAppliedOut.title: SignalAppliedOut

SignalExclusionsOut.description:
Why rows did not reach the table.

Every dropped row is counted under the first reason that applies to it. Unknown is
its own bucket: an unknown value is never counted as a zero that failed a filter.
SignalExclusionsOut.title: SignalExclusionsOut

SignalMoverOut.description: One ranked mover. The change is the window's own price change, as a decimal string.
SignalMoverOut.title: SignalMoverOut

SignalMoversOut.description:
The movers read model for one window and one direction.

An empty ``rows`` list carries a ``reason`` code. No mover is invented to fill it.
SignalMoversOut.title: SignalMoversOut

StoredMarketListOut.description: One page of persisted observations with the same paging contract as live rows.
StoredMarketListOut.title: StoredMarketListOut

StoredSnapshotOut.description:
A persisted token observation with the contract's source and read-time age.

``source`` is null when the row carries no usable provenance (a blank name or the
writer's ``unknown`` sentinel), and then ``age_seconds`` and ``stale`` are null too:
there is no observation to age, and an unprovenanced row is never reported as fresh.
StoredSnapshotOut.title: StoredSnapshotOut

StrategyPerformanceOut.description:
PAPER performance for one strategy, from the account ledger.

``realized_pnl_usd`` is net of fees and books a buy fee when the ledger pays it.
``market_value_usd`` is the strategy's contribution to account equity. An unknown
mark leaves ``market_value_usd`` and ``unrealized_pnl_usd`` null and sets
``complete`` false; it is never valued at zero.
StrategyPerformanceOut.title: StrategyPerformanceOut

StrategyPolicyOut.description:
One strategy's effective policy: its override or the deployment default.

``source`` names where the profile came from, never a guess. ``warnings`` lists the
strategy's own sizing that the profile's resolver would reject, so a row cannot claim
a size it cannot trade.
StrategyPolicyOut.title: StrategyPolicyOut

StrategyRiskPolicyIn.description: A partial per-strategy override. ``null`` returns the strategy to the default.
StrategyRiskPolicyIn.title: StrategyRiskPolicyIn

TokenOut.description:
Token header whose source and age come from the contract, not the adapter.

``age_seconds`` is measured at read time from ``source``. ``stale`` is the contract's
verdict at the same clock; when there is no source the age is null and ``stale`` is
``False`` because the token page treats a missing observation as unknown, not stale.
TokenOut.title: TokenOut

TokenPerformanceOut.description:
Per-token projection from ledger groups and the latest known mark.

``realized_usd`` is net of fees, because the ledger books each fee as its own leg.
``fees_usd`` is shown separately for transparency and is not additive to it.
TokenPerformanceOut.title: TokenPerformanceOut

TradePolicyOut.description: Every profile, the caller's active policy, and each strategy's effective policy.
TradePolicyOut.title: TradePolicyOut

TradePolicyPreviewOut.description: The server's sizing verdict for one proposed buy under one profile.
TradePolicyPreviewOut.title: TradePolicyPreviewOut

WatchlistIn.description: A watched token identity. No price, route or balance may be supplied.
WatchlistIn.title: WatchlistIn

WatchlistMissingOut.description: A watched token with no matching market row; unknown, never dropped.
WatchlistMissingOut.title: WatchlistMissingOut

info.description: Live market browsing and paper execution. No keys, no live money.
info.title: ezCHAIN API

get.description:
Every agent whose owner set a cap, with the deployment replayed from the ledger.

An agent key sees its own bucket only. A failure to read the journal is a typed ``409``
rather than an empty list: an empty list would read as "nothing is capped", which is the
one answer this surface must not invent. The refusal carries its own message and never
the driver's, which can name a DSN.
One bucket. Another agent's id and a never-minted id answer identically.

put.description: Set one agent's cap. Only the agent's owner, and only a person, may.

get.description: What an agent may do on this deployment, before it calls a single tool.

get.description:
The new-pairs feed for one chain, or every registered chain.

The answer is bounded: at most ``DISCOVERY_CANDIDATE_ROWS`` discovery rows are ranked
and at most ``DISCOVERY_MAX_ROWS`` rows are returned. The response carries the coverage
of the pass — candidates, deduped, per-reason drops and whether the page was cut — plus
the source and the read clock.
The one node table the editor renders. Read-only and deterministic.

schema.title: Response Get Catalogue Api V1 Graph Catalogue Get

post.description: Evaluate one tick against live data. Never places an order.

schema.title: Response Dry Run Api V1 Graph Dry Run Post

post.description:
Compile a document.

A well-formed JSON object always returns 200 with the full report — an invalid graph
is a normal, editable state for the builder. Only a missing/non-object ``graph`` is a
422, because there is nothing to validate.

schema.title: Response Validate Graph Api V1 Graph Validate Post

get.description: What this process can see right now, one row per registered chain.

The paper account as a pure ledger projection.

Read-only by construction: genesis and the wallet declarations are bootstrapped at
boot and on order placement, so this route never creates a row. A missing wallet is
reported as missing (its cash appears in the unallocated bucket) instead of being
healed by the read that is supposed to expose it.
Derived operator alerts. Empty list means the account is clean.

The queue, newest first. An agent key may read it; it shows who decided what.

A ``pending`` row past its window reports ``expired`` without this read writing
anything, and a stored status that is not one of the declared values reports
``failed`` rather than being read as pending.

schema.title: Response List Approvals Api V1 Paper Approvals Get

post.description:
Approve the stored order and execute it, through the normal paper path.

The body may carry a note; it may not carry an order. What executes is what the agent
proposed and the server stored, so an approval cannot be widened into a different
trade. Refusals keep their reason code: an expired approval, an already-decided one,
and a principal that is not a person each answer with their own code.
Refuse the stored order with the person's own reason.

get.description: Per-token realized PnL and its share of absolute realized PnL.

schema.title: Response Attribution Api V1 Paper Attribution Get

get.description: This user's automation tier. A new user is ``manual``: agent orders wait.

put.description:
Switch the tier. Only a person may, and ``full_auto`` needs the acknowledgement.

The acknowledgement is persisted as an append-only consent row naming the user, the
disclosure version and the moment; returning to ``manual`` leaves that history in
place. A refused change writes nothing.

get.description: Newest-first fills. ``offset`` pages past the newest ``limit`` rows.

schema.title: Response Fill History Api V1 Paper Fills Get

get.description: Newest-first journal slice, filterable by account and kind, pageable by offset.

schema.title: Response Ledger Entries Api V1 Paper Ledger Get

get.description: The risk limits the UI may show, plus the persisted operator switch.
Newest-first orders. ``offset`` pages past the newest ``limit`` rows.

schema.title: Response Order History Api V1 Paper Orders Get

get.description: PAPER cash, equity, realized/unrealized PnL, trade counts and daily realized.

schema.title: Response Positions Api V1 Paper Positions Get

get.description: Read-only proof that the journal, fills and orders agree.

Every paper wallet with the cash the ledger has settled to it.

Read-only: the declared wallets are seeded at boot and on order placement, and a
wallet is a view over the journal whose balance does not exist as a stored number.
The route never writes, so a read cannot change what the next read sees. Cash whose
attributed wallet row is gone is reported in a final ``unallocated`` row with a null
id, so the rows always add up to the account's cash instead of dropping it.

schema.title: Response Wallets Api V1 Paper Wallets Get

Store a user-supplied key and return its fingerprint, not the key.

One key is active per provider. A second create is a 409 unless ``replace`` is set,
which retires the previous key through the revoke path before storing the new one.

schema.title: Response Create Provider Key Api V1 Provider Keys Post

get.description:
The ranked movers for one window and one direction.

The answer is bounded: at most ``SIGNALS_CANDIDATE_ROWS`` discovery rows are ranked
and at most ``SIGNALS_MAX_ROWS`` movers are returned. Every row carries its source,
its observation time and its age. A read that produces no mover returns an empty
list with a reason code instead of a fabricated row.

schema.title: Response List Strategies Api V1 Strategies Get

get.description: Paper-gate evidence for an owner decision. This endpoint never promotes.

schema.title: Response Strategy Live Readiness Api V1 Strategies  Strategy Id  Live Readiness Get

get.description: PAPER performance from this strategy's own fills, never the whole account.

post.description:
Run one cycle now, at the owner's explicit request.

Pause gates automatic scheduling, not a manual run: a paused strategy executes this
one cycle (even inside its interval) and stays paused, so the scheduler keeps
skipping it afterwards. Resuming separately is what re-enables scheduling.

schema.title: Response Strategy Runs Api V1 Strategies  Strategy Id  Runs Get

get.description: Signed-provenance verdict for this installation, with the reason for a refusal.
Operator switch with two levels over one flag. Persisted in ``system_flags``.

post.description:
Arm or release the switch.

Mutating routes require ``Authorization: Bearer <EZCHAIN_API_TOKEN>`` (middleware);
the response carries the persisted state and ``updated_at`` (the audit timestamp).
The token identifies the deployment, not an individual operator.

get.description:
Closed OHLCV history for one token, oldest bar first.
Read-only and unauthenticated like every other GET. The series is served from
``market_candles`` when it is current; only a missing range reaches the provider.
Every profile, its fields, and each strategy's effective policy.
Check one proposed buy against a profile with the order gate's resolver.

put.description: Set or clear one strategy's profile, with acknowledgement at a loosening.

schema.title: Response Remove From Watchlist Api V1 Watchlist Delete
Response List Watchlist Api V1 Watchlist Get

post.description: Add once. A repeat returns the same row with the same 200, never a duplicate.

get.description: Compatibility health endpoint: 503 when the database is down.

Liveness: the process is up. Never touches the database.

The mode is the same derived value the capabilities document reports, so a probe and
an agent cannot disagree about whether this deployment can trade.

Prometheus text exposition with bounded labels. No third-party dependency.

A loopback scrape needs no credential; a scrape from another host sends the
deployment token (middleware). The operational families are sampled from live state;
when the database cannot be read they are omitted rather than reported as zero.

Readiness: database reachable and schema exactly at the Alembic head.

The desktop build bootstraps its embedded SQLite schema with ``create_all`` and has no
Alembic revision row. That is a supported deployment mode, not a missing migration;
it reports ``migration: embedded`` and is ready once the database answers.
